one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban surveys the stunning 2016 US presidential election: Hillary Clinton -- 'buoyed by poll surveys, acclaimed by the media, bankrolled by Wall Street and propelled by a formidable electoral machine' -- won the popular vote but lost the antiquated Electoral College to Donald Trump, the oldest and first outsider-president, and patriotically conceded like fellow Democrat Al Gore in 2000. For the first time in memory, a US election will radically alter US foreign policy, as the political novice with no public-office experience defied political correctness, overrode party leaders, and convinced his compatriots that he alone could 'make America great again.' The electorate ignored his catalog of disqualifying behaviors -- vulgarity, buffoonery, sexual perversion, tax-dodging issues, lies, bullying, insults, refusal to release tax returns, and bias against blacks, Muslims, Mexicans, Latinos, and Asians -- viewing him as less objectionable than Clinton's email imponderables, Obamacare support, and continuation of foreign adventurism. Trump's 'America first' platform was beguilingly simple: pep up the economy, give jobs to locals, lower taxes, end the US role as world policeman, stop massive foreign aid, bill allies for defense, befriend Russia, toughen immigration, and rebalance trade -- implemented through protectionism (ban or heavily tax foreign goods), required citizen employment, and an end to outsourcing. This reverses the very WTO free-trade framework America itself initiated in the last century to expand markets -- a framework that backfired when Germany/Japan outproduced US industrials and China became 'the world's favorite factory,' demolishing local US industries. For the Philippines, Trump's protectionism will harm the economy in two insidious ways: (1) outsourcing taxes will dry up the BPO industry that employed 1M+ Filipinos and generated $22B in 2015; (2) professional/blue-collar restrictions + merciless deportation will dent OFW remittances ($25B in 2015) -- and these inflows are 'the backbone of our economy' with multiplier effects in real estate, housing, food, transportation, and entertainment. In sum, Trump's promises 'will presage a regime of vulgarity, unorthodoxy and hostility that will erode the era of urbanity, predictability and liberty with dire domino consequences in the Philippines and the rest of the world.'
